headline_marked: Thakurgaon-1 by-poll: [[Jamaat candidate claims presiding officers lack photo IDs]]
headline: Thakurgaon-1 by-poll: Jamaat candidate claims presiding officers lack photo IDs
summary: Md Delwar Hossain alleges irregularities as voting begins across 185 polling stations in the constituency.
details: Voting is underway in the Thakurgaon-1 constituency by-election, with 516,140 voters choosing from five candidates. Polling began at 8am on Thursday across 185 stations and is scheduled to continue until 4pm.

Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami candidate Md Delwar Hossain raised concerns after casting his vote at Adarsha School. He claimed that presiding officers and assistant presiding officers were wearing identification cards without photos, making it difficult to verify their identities.
Delwar expressed worry that the lack of photo IDs could allow proxies to serve as election officials. He also alleged that polling agents from his party had been removed from one or two centers.

Despite these complaints, the Returning Officer and Thakurgaon District Election Officer Kamrul Islam stated that voting is proceeding peacefully across all 185 centers and that no official complaints had been received.
The candidates competing for the seat include Mirza Faisal Amin, Md Delwar Hossain, Md Abdul Alim Nizami, Hafez Md Khademul Islam, and Hussain Muhammad Omar Farooq.
Delwar stated he is confident of winning if the election is fair and impartial, adding that he will accept any result of the democratic process if the vote is free.

headline_marked: Japan visit: [[PM Tarique Rahman visits Toyota’s Motomachi plant]]
headline: Japan visit: PM Tarique Rahman visits Toyota’s Motomachi plant
summary: The Prime Minister toured the vehicle assembly process and was briefed on manufacturing stages during the final day of his official visit to Japan.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Toyota’s Motomachi factory in Nagoya, Japan, on Thursday morning.
During the tour, the prime minister and his entourage observed the vehicle assembly process and received briefings on the various stages of manufacturing.
Senior Toyota officials, including Masahiko Moeda (CEO for South Asia region), Shigeru Harada (CEO of Mobility Division at Toyota Tsusho Corporation), and Shinichiro Otsuka (COO), were present.
The prime minister was accompanied by his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, and State Minister Aninda Islam Amit.
Also present were Advisor Rehan Asif Asad, Special Assistant Md Shakirul Islam Khan, Additional Press Secretary Atiqur Rahman Ruman, and Research Officer Abdus Sattar Patwary.
caption:
From assembly lines to manufacturing briefings—PM Tarique Rahman explores Toyota's Motomachi plant in Japan.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited Toyota’s Motomachi factory in Nagoya, Japan, on Thursday morning.

During the tour, the prime minister and his entourage observed the vehicle assembly process and received briefings on the various stages of manufacturing.

Senior Toyota officials, including Masahiko Moeda (CEO for South Asia region), Shigeru Harada (CEO of Mobility Division at Toyota Tsusho Corporation), and Shinichiro Otsuka (COO), were present.

The prime minister was accompanied by his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman, Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat, and State Minister Aninda Islam Amit.

Also present were Advisor Rehan Asif Asad, Special Assistant Md Shakirul Islam Khan, Additional Press Secretary Atiqur Rahman Ruman, and Research Officer Abdus Sattar Patwary.
